title: design gap (T3, T6). On vblanks, the real picture of a step is almost never shown, and every step costs one extra unseen walk.
note: Design (read 11-18, E6a, file F G2 part 1): start_interp_sequence gives a lead only off vblanks (locked = !on_vblanks && rate a multiple of 60); on vblanks lead is 0 and the slots follow the display, so t = 1 falls between refreshes and the real picture's walk is made and never shown (5 to 13 of 2,640 steps shown). The step is phased to the display on every host (Windows: FramePhase in svc_frame_wait aims the step at a vblank; SDL: wait_display_frame), so at refresh = k x 60 within 0.2 % (vblanks_per_slot 1 and rate/60 whole) the sequence takes lead 1/k with its slot clock anchored at the vblank nearest the arrival: slots show t = 1/k .. 1, the last the real picture, and no walk is thrown away. Needs I-013 first (FramePhase measures the step's own work) so the phase holds under in-between pictures. Other rates keep lead 0 until passes name what they read (file F). Proof: real pictures shown, counted as file F section 1A did, at 120 and 240 Hz near every step (today 5 to 13 of 2,640), walks per step k (today k + 1), pace.py animation_within_1ms unchanged. 11-19 (FRAME-MODEL 2.16, E6b read at 241395b49 and rows/i016 697535a86): placed in E6b's landing 2; 2.16's rows table says what it does for this row.

title: wrong behaviour (T4). Interpolation adds about one to two steps of latency, and neither camera nor pointer is sampled at present time.
note: Design (read 11-18, E6a's first change, file F G1): the step-moment arrival and its slow delay tracking are in (render_core.cpp start_interp_sequence); what still costs the step is the gate on the present. The game submits list N at its frame end (host_main.cpp svc_submit_frame, present false) and asks for its present only at frame N+1's start (svc_frame_begun -> submit_frame(true, black), NebulaFrameClock onFrame); the render thread holds the list (interp_list_waiting_) until that chunk comes, about 15 ms later. The only reason to wait is black, and black is set only around a restart (NebulaFrameClock::show: GameSystemObjHolder true, GameSystemRestartProcess false). New: svc_submit_frame marks the list's chunk shown when the frame clock shows a picture and the start is not skipping frames (gBootFast); such a chunk starts its sequence when its walk is done (the arrival its own step moment plus the tracked delay, as now), and the next frame's present only supersedes it when it is black; a chunk not marked waits as today. Changed in play: at a restart the last list before black can be shown for up to a step (the console never showed it). Proof: pace.py at 240 Hz with in-between pictures on, delay_avg_us before and after (file F: 42.4 ms to about 26), the timeline's RenderBegin to first present; pictures and replays the same in fixed-step tests. 11-19 (FRAME-MODEL 2.16, E6b read at 241395b49 and rows/i016 697535a86): placed in E6b's landing 1; 2.16's rows table says what it does for this row.

title: wrong behaviour (T2, T7). Linux has no display clock.
note: Design (read 11-18): Linux gets the display clock from the presents themselves. The Vulkan renderer already makes its swap chain with present ids and present wait (VK_KHR_present_id2/present_wait2, renderer_vk.cpp), which Mesa and NVIDIA's driver give on X11 and Wayland: a waiter thread waits on each present id and stamps when it completed; the stamps fitted to the mode's period (SDL_GetCurrentDisplayMode, refined by the stamps' median spacing) are the vblank grid display_clock.cpp hands the slots, as the Choreographer's are on Android. Where VK_EXT_present_timing is offered, its present-stage times and refresh duration take that place. No grid (no present wait) keeps today's clock. Proof: Linux at 144 Hz with present-stats: the vblank-steps histogram filled, no two pictures in one refresh over 3000 pictures; a unit test of the fit fed stamps with jitter and a missed refresh. 11-19 (FRAME-MODEL 2.16, E6b read at 241395b49 and rows/i016 697535a86): placed in E6b's landing 3; 2.16's rows table says what it does for this row.

title: wrong behaviour (T2), suspected. Metal drops a picture when `nextDrawable` waited more than 1.5 ms.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed as a guess where a count is available. renderer_mtl.mm present: with VSync on, a frame whose nextDrawable took more than kDrawableWaitMs (1.5 ms) is not handed over (held_last_, never two frames running), to take one queued picture out of the layer's line. The wait time stands in for the line's length: a wake-up late by scheduling, a display link phase or a ProMotion rate change waits as long with an empty line, and that frame is lost (a visible skip). The renderer already adds a presented handler to every drawable (the pacing recorder). Design: count drawables handed over and not yet presented (up at presentDrawable, down in the presented handler, presentedTime 0 included) and hold a picture back only when that count is 2 or more at the moment the drawable comes; the wait time is no longer read. Proof: Mac run with --diagnostics timeline, a test hook that delays the render thread by 2 ms every 30th frame: no picture held before the count says the line is full (pictures_held_ 0), the start's queued pictures still drained (latency at hand-over as now). 11-19 (FRAME-MODEL 2.16, E6b read at 241395b49 and rows/i016 697535a86): placed in E6b's landing 3; 2.16's rows table says what it does for this row.

title: wrong behaviour (T2), suspected. VRR detection and slot timing.
note: Design (read 11-18, E6a; renderer_common.h next_variable_refresh, renderer_d3d12.cpp refresh_display_rate): variable refresh is not inferred from the vblank thread's rate (that rate follows the presents once it is on, and near the mode rate it never falls under 0.8 of it). It is asked of the system where it answers (Vulkan VK_EXT_present_timing / display timing where present; Apple: the display link's minimum and maximum rates, ProMotion) and proved from the presents everywhere: with presents held at a rate between the mode and half of it (variable_refresh_cap), a fixed-rate display shows each picture for whole mode periods (DXGI frame statistics: PresentRefreshCount steps of 1 and 2), a variable one for the presents' own interval (steps follow the presents, SyncQPCTime intervals equal the present intervals). The test runs on the frame statistics already read (DisplayStats events), at the first seconds after a display change, and its answer holds until the next change. When variable: the slots follow the arrival clock at the cap (the present pacer's QPC clock), never the vblank thread's grid, so the slot clock and the display no longer feed each other; VSync stays on with tearing allowed above the range. The same on D3D11 and Vulkan (their callers of next_variable_refresh). Proof: a VRR monitor (or the tablet's 120 Hz LTPO panel, Vulkan) with the timeline: VBlank against PresentEnd, the variable state, and even spacing of new pictures at 144 Hz with two in-between pictures; I-016's scheduler tests get the decision as a unit (statistics in, answer out) with fixed and variable sequences. 11-19 (FRAME-MODEL 2.16, E6b read at 241395b49 and rows/i016 697535a86): placed in E6b's landing 3; 2.16's rows table says what it does for this row. 11-23 (AG cards, the planner's decisions): the nine points the design left unsaid are written into G2.3 with their sources: below the range's lowest rate (the pacer repeats nothing; no maker's page gives the lowest rate on the paths read), the cap (no maker's page gives a figure; the margin is measured, 99.9th percentile of the precise wait's lateness, the code's mode less mode squared over 3600 being the start value), `refresh` in G2.5's bound is the cap, the step is never locked under variable refresh (`step_lock_refreshes` takes the variable answer), composed or tearing-less windows answer fixed with five events that ask again, Android says variable only by `Display.hasArrSupport()` (API 36) and shows no picture off its grid, Linux by `VK_EXT_present_timing`'s `refreshInterval` or the stamps, proof 5 rewritten, the settings texts' files named. G2.2's lead reads the slot clock so that it takes the pacer's rate.

title: design gap (T6), suspected. Two governors act on the same GPU time without knowing of each other.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed in code. Dynamic resolution (renderer_d3d12.cpp, once per scene picture) aims the scene pictures' GPU time at resolution_budget_ms(present_frame_rate(cap, VSync, refresh)), the display's rate; the interpolation governor (render_core.cpp interp_gpu_governor) picks k generated pictures a step from interpolation_gpu_cost_ms against 0.9 of a step and runs the slot clock at 60 x (k + 1). Neither reads the other: with k capped below the display's rate the pictures come at 60 x (k + 1) while dynamic resolution budgets 1/refresh, so it lowers the resolution further than the rate in use needs; the cheaper pictures then let the interpolation governor raise k after 2 s, which tightens the real budget again, a slow loop between the two (dynamic resolution steps up after 60 pictures, k after 120 sequences). Design: one controller owns both (k, sixteenths) against one budget, the slot period in use: the display's rate is filled first (k up to refresh/60 - 1) at no less than the resolution floor, then resolution rises in the time left; over budget, resolution falls to the floor before k falls. Proof: a unit test of the controller fed measured costs (a heavy scene at 144 Hz: one stable (k, sixteenths), no alternation over 3000 pictures); then the run the audit asks for, [dynres] and [interp-stats] gpu-generated-cap on a heavy galaxy at 144 Hz. 11-19 (FRAME-MODEL 2.16, E6b read at 241395b49 and rows/i016 697535a86): placed in E6b's landing 5; 2.16's rows table says what it does for this row.

title: design gap (T7). Only Android Vulkan presents at a requested time; only Windows has frame telemetry and the timeline.
note: Read 11-18: the timeline is Windows only in code, not just in use: frame_timeline.h's now() returns 0 and initialize()/dump() are empty outside _WIN32, so --diagnostics timeline on Android, Linux or Mac writes nothing (luma_test_android.py asks for it anyway). Design: the POSIX side with clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) in nanoseconds (the header's frequency field says 1e9, so tools/perf/timeline_digest.py is unchanged), gettid, and a plain file write at the orderly exit the host already calls; Apple the same with mach_absolute_time and its timebase. It comes first in E3 (the tablet trace needs it). Test: a unit test in tests/unit (Linux runs it) that records, dumps and reads back the header and records. The other half (present at a requested time on more platforms) is E6b's. 11-19 (FRAME-MODEL 2.16, E6b read at 241395b49 and rows/i016 697535a86): placed in E6b's landing 3; 2.16's rows table says what it does for this row.

title: wrong behaviour (minor), suspected. FramePhase measures the wrong work under interpolation.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed, as the audit (E) says. host_main.cpp next_frame_start takes a step's work as g_last_present_ns minus the previous step's start; RenderCore stamps g_last_present_ns only for a real picture (render_core.cpp, note_picture_shown when `real`). With in-between pictures on, a step's real picture is shown about two steps after the step, or never (I-002), so work is that arrival delay or 0 (the budget left as it was), and the phase aims at vblank - (delay + 1.5 ms), not at the step's own work. Design: the measure is keyed by the step: the render thread records, for each frame index, when that step's list was taken and its picture rendered (one slot per frame index, written beside the timeline's SubmitEnd and RenderSubmitted), and next_frame_start reads the entry of the step that started at previous_ns, with or without in-between pictures. Proof: a unit test of the measure fed a step rendered at +5 ms whose real picture is shown at +30 ms: work 5 ms (before: 30 ms or 0); and the timeline at 120 Hz with interpolation, StepWaitEnd against VBlank. 11-19 (FRAME-MODEL 2.16, E6b read at 241395b49 and rows/i016 697535a86): placed in E6b's landing 1; 2.16's rows table says what it does for this row.

title: wrong behaviour (T2), suspected. Game-declared camera cuts come from two places only.
note: Read 11-18: confirmed in code. MotionSignal::cameraCut fires only in CameraViewInterpolator::reduceOscillation when mIsForceCameraChange (setInterpolation(0)) and at CameraAnim cut frames. CameraDirector::isInterpolationOff also counts a camera man that declares its own interpolation off (CameraManEvent::isInterpolationOff, an event camera that snaps): that switch is instant but sends no cut, so the host's heuristic (60 degrees, or 1500 units and 6x the last move) decides, and a snap to a near angle is blended for one step. FrameList writes camera_epoch (sCuts) and nothing reads it: the host reads NEBULA_FRAME_CAMERA_CUT. Design: the cut is sent where the game decides a camera does not interpolate: CameraDirector::switchAntiOscillation when isInterpolationOff() (both causes), CameraAnim's cut frames as now, and the director's restart paths after a warp or a scene start; camera_epoch leaves the frame list (one signal, the flag). Proof: the tour's present-stats with in-between pictures on: game-cuts against camera-cuts at pipes, doors and event cameras (every heuristic cut there also a game cut), generated pictures at a door with no blend, and the step-hash replay the same (the signal is not game state). 11-19 (FRAME-MODEL 2.16, E6b read at 241395b49 and rows/i016 697535a86): placed in E6b's landing 7; 2.16's rows table says what it does for this row.

title: (stability and latency on Android's host): the event pump sleeps a fixed 8 ms when no event is waiting (host_window_sdl.cpp:1194-1204, called with 8 at host_main.cpp:6573), so touch, pad and window events and queued requests wait up to that long; the display clock's sleep retries on any error of clock_nanosleep, not only EINTR (display_clock.cpp:155-157), so an EINVAL spins its thread for good; the surface hand-over goes on after 2 s with the renderer still holding the surface (host_window_sdl.cpp:1670-1679; the renderers check surface_withdrawn before each acquire, renderer_vk.cpp:2991, :2996); the Wii Remote link reads its JNI table unlocked (wiimote_link_android.cpp:73, :80, :117-118, :130, :133) while nativeInit writes it under s.lock (:175-188).
note: Found by the readall harness's platform/sdl report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Fixes: the pump blocks on a wait an event or a queued request wakes (an SDL event watch signalling a condition); the sleep retries only on EINTR and otherwise hands back to the host's clock; past the 2 s the device-lost path runs rather than the surface going under a present; the JNI table published once through an atomic pointer (release, read with acquire). Replay identical.

title: (untested on a real display, every system) no display of ours shows an Android refresh rate that is not a multiple of 60, or a real variable-refresh display on Linux or on the Mac

What we have, read 11-23: the PC's monitor, an Odyssey G8 by its own name, 3840 by 2160 at 240 Hz (whether its adaptive sync is switched on is not read by any file; G2.3 proof 5 reads it); the tablet SM-X810 lists 120, 60 and 30 Hz modes and no other (read by the planner from dumpsys display). What that run's log must show: [pace] lines whose refresh_ms is the display's period (13.333 at 75 Hz), steps_per_second 60.00, missed=0 and doubled=0, animation_within_1ms near 1.0; on a variable display the timeline's variable state and presents spaced by the cap; and the benchmark result's device refresh_hz (null where no display grid is known).
